summary: Periodic 5xx bursts caused by thread-allocator imbalance leading to runtime aborts
description:
Issue summary:
Customers (notably BrightDocs, enterprise tier) reported intermittent 5xx errors on chat and embeddings routes from ~2026-03-10 02:30 UTC onward. Errors present as short bursts (~30s–3m) recurring every ~10–20 minutes. High-level symptoms: apigateway returns 502/503 to clients; runtime processes in the affected shard show recent process aborts with SIGABRT; ephemeral proxy (accept/handoff) shows long syscall latencies and accept-queue growth.

Impact:
- Multiple BrightDocs endpoints experienced degraded availability: ~6% p50->p95 error rate spike during bursts, impacting customer SLAs.
- Several other customers in us-east-1 saw transient elevated 5xx rates (non-global).

Observed timeline (local):
- 02:30 UTC: first client reports; apigw error-rate graph (dash/apigw/errors/us-east) shows spike.
- 02:33 UTC: runtime shard node-14 reported SIGABRT and restarted.
- 02:34–02:36 UTC: ephemeral-proxy accept-queue length increased from <50 to ~1200.
- 02:40 UTC: errors subside; runtimes stabilize after automatic respawn.
- Pattern repeated every ~12 minutes for the following 3 hours.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Simulate steady small-payload streaming + intermittent large-embedding bulk on a tenant in us-east-1.
2) Observe accept-queue growth when embed bulk starts at moderate concurrency (~100 concurrently).
3) After ~30–90s of accept-queue pressure, runtimes exhibit high thread creation latency and occasional aborts.

Key logs/snippets:
- runtime stderr: "pthread_create: Resource temporarily unavailable" followed by immediate abort/backtrace.
- dmesg: no OOM killer entries for GPU memory; kernel reporting short-lived thread creation failures.
- ephemeral-proxy metrics: "accept_queue_wait_seconds_p90" jumps to 8s.

Customer impact note: BrightDocs support rep escalated at 03:05 UTC (ticket #BD-221). They asked for ETA and suggested rate-limiting until root cause fixed.

Expected next actions requested by customer: temporary rate limit on heavy-embedding routes; patch and hotfix to runtime if allocator tuning required.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: not a GPU OOM or kernel-level fd exhaustion. Multiple signals point to userland thread allocator/backpressure:
- Repeated "pthread_create" errors inside the runtime process indicate a thread creation failure path rather than file-descriptor exhaustion. FD counts appear within normal ranges.
- Profiling (perf + pstack from coredump) shows runtime stuck in allocator_mmap/arena_lock in jemalloc build path when under accept-queue pressure.
- Ephemeral-proxy exhibited long handoff latencies which increased backlog and caused sudden bursts of concurrent short-lived work items in runtimes; combined with an aggressive thread-creation policy this appears to trigger a resource starvation loop.
- Stress test reproducer created with workload-mix script reproduces the SIGABRT within ~90s when threadpool target is set to 'unbounded' (current default on this shard).

Hypothesis: A combination of accept-queue surge + runtime threadpool unbounded growth + contention inside the chosen allocator (jemalloc) results in failed pthread_create and aborts. On restart, the runtime briefly recovers then the pattern repeats.

Evidence/Artifacts:
- Slack thread: #support (link: https://slack.redwood/support/thread/S-984)
- Dashboards: dash/apigw/errors/us-east (spike graphs), dash/runtime/thread-create-failures/node-14
- Collected coredump: /artifacts/coredump/node-14/2026-03-10-02-33 (uploaded to s3://rbw-incident-coreruns/707707/)
- Reproducer: scripts/reproducers/thread-surge-mix.sh (run under infra/sim cluster)
comments: 2026-03-10 03:12 - Maya Chen (Support): Filed after initial customer escalation. Noted pattern looked different from previous 'keepalive-flood' incidents due to pthread_create failures.

2026-03-10 03:27 - Rajat Singh (SRE): Confirmed coredump shows abort triggered by assert in runtime: 'pthread_create() failed'. Starting controlled repro on staging with same allocator build. Link to staging run: https://ci.redwood/repro/707707-01

2026-03-10 04:05 - Evi Park (Backend Eng): Observed high jemalloc arena mutex hold times under stress. Suggest temporarily constraining threadpool growth and disabling unbounded worker spin on affected shard. Will open PR for runtime config change.
2026-03-10 05:20 - CS Rep (BrightDocs): Requested immediate mitigation (rate limiting) and asked for ETA on hotfix. Logged in BD support portal.

2026-03-11 09:10 - Rajat Singh: Applied emergency config (limit runtime worker_threads max=256) on shard node-14 and neighboring nodes; saw a reduction in frequency and severity of 5xx bursts. Monitoring continuing.
2026-03-12 11:00 - Eng Lead (Priya Rao): Performance patch to allocator parameters approved (PR #4212). Schedule hotpatch during low-traffic window 2026-03-12 23:00 UTC.
resolution:
Temporary mitigation: limited runtime worker_threads to 256 on affected shard families and applied an accept-queue backpressure parameter to ephemeral-proxy (handshake-window=30ms). This immediately reduced pthread_create failures and lowered 5xx burst amplitude.

Planned permanent fix: merge PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4212 which adds: (a) jemalloc tuning (reduced arenas + less aggressive trimming), (b) bounded threadpool policy with exponential backoff for short-lived tasks, (c) improved logging on thread_create failures to avoid immediate abort.

Rollout notes: hotpatch scheduled 2026-03-12 23:00 UTC; phased rollout across us-east-1 shards with canary on node-14 then +4 nodes. Post-deploy smoke tests include acceptance-scenarios/stream-embed-mix and 30m soak.

Customer follow-up: BrightDocs notified of mitigations and upcoming fix; offer of dedicated postmortem and longer-term SLA credit under review.
